answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a shared reputation score. The score updates only after counterparties complete transactions, and disputed outcomes can slash the bond, so creating a nebula of identities does not multiply influence for free. An attacker must lock up capital for every persona and risks losing it when agents collude or default; this raises the cost of a sybil campaign while leaving honest agents free to build trust over time, whether they trade across a bridge or on a terrace.
